assembly_info.comments:
Background:
The Physarum polycephalum genomic DNA was extracted from axenic, haploid amoebal cells (strain LU352 developed in Jennifer Dee's laboratory, Leicester University). Cell culturing and DNA sampling was carried out by Gerard Pierron and Marianne Benard (Institut Andre Lwoff, Villejuif, France).
Total assembled sequence coverage of Roche 454 instrument reads was 54.6X (fragments, 3kb, and 8kb), and the genome spanned over 190Mb. The combined sequence reads were assembled using the Newbler software, version 2.6 (Life Technologies, Roche). The Newbler assembled contigs were scaffolded using Bambus v2.3 (Pop et al 2004), and a transcriptome-guided scaffolding algorithm (X. Chen and L. Landweber, Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, Princeton University). This draft assembly was referred to as Physarum polycephalum 10.0. In this version the assembly has been cleaned of contaminating contigs. All scaffolds of at least 200 bases were retained for submission to the public databases. The assembly is made up of a total of 69,709 scaffolds with an N50 scaffold length of nearly 54kb (N50 contig length was 2.2kb).

The National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI), National Institutes of Health (NIH) have provided the Genome Institute at Washington University School of Medicine funding for sequence and characterization of the Physarum polycephalum genome. The individual reads for this project are available from the NCBI trace archive.

For questions regarding this Physarum polycephalum 10.0 assembly please contact Patrick Minx, Washington University School of Medicine (pminx@genome.wustl.edu).
